text:
Inside real safety, people can turn the polarity dial all the way to the right.

Fantasy is one of the best ways to experiment with that. Domination fantasies are common in many forms, and they enable extreme masculine-feminine polarity without actual harm, because the real person still has consent and can stop.

Nobody is entitled to another person’s fantasies. They’re private until the person decides to share one, and when somebody does, it can be an extraordinary act of trust.

Esther Perel makes the distinction that fantasy is play rather than a real-life request. So someone with a rape fantasy isn’t asking to actually be raped.

A couple can keep a fantasy in their heads, or they can agree to act some part of it out.

Fantasy should also add to arousal, not be the only way to get there, because I want to be able to enjoy the actual woman and the actual experience too.
reader: Someone with a fantasy they haven’t shared, deciding whether and how to bring it to a partner.

(adjunct remedy; known-genuine) Is every term a high-school graduate wouldn't know (enterocytes, BPC-157) explained once, where it is first used, and common ones (a vitamin) left alone?
